newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
NO QUESTION OF QUITTING, SAYS BIHAR CHIEF MINISTER

Bihar chief minister Laloo Yadav firmly stuck to his decision not to resign in the wake of the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) formally seeking the governor's approval to prosecute him in the animal husbandry scandal. A defiant Yadav said it was neither the opposition nor the CBI which made him chief minister, and that he would continue to hold office as long as legislators and the people of the state had confidence in him.
The Economic Times
COKE'S FOUR NEW DOWNSTREAM PROJECTS APPROVED

Coca Cola's proposal to operationalise four new downstream subsidiaries has been approved by the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB). These would be initially set up as 100 percent subsidiaries with the condition that they would divest up to 49 percent over a period of five years. Earlier the government gave Coca Cola's South Asia Holdings approval to set up two wholly-owned subsidiaries as holding companies for bringing in foreign capital for investing in production and distribution of non-alcoholic beverages. Each of the subsidiaries was permitted to be capitalised over a period of 10 years with foreign equity of up to $350 million each.
RANBAXY, U.S. FIRM NOT TO MAKE DRUGS

Ranbaxy Laboratories and Elli Lilly of the U.S. have dropped plans to carry out manufacturing activities through their research, development and manufacturing joint venture in India. Ranbaxy officials said the 50:50 joint venture company would not set up a manufacturing plant of its own, at least not in the next three to four years. The joint venture was formed in 1995 essentially to manufacture bulk drugs for the U.S. market.
Financial Express
PAL PEUGEOT SEEKS IMPORT LICENCE

Pal Peugeot, the joint venture company of Premier Automobiles and Automobiles Peugeot of France has sought an ad hoc licence to import 6,000 completely knocked down (CKD) kits for the 309 model during 1997/98. This urgent request was made to the Directorate General Of Foreign Trade while waiting for the import licensee to ship 18,000 CKD kits into the country. The ad hoc licence is absolutely essential for PAL Peugeot which was fast running out of kits at its Bombay warehouse. The present supply will not last beyond June this year. During 1995/96, the company's import licenee allowed it to ship 5,000 kits to the country.
CENTURY TEXTILES, OTHERS WAIT WITH BATED BREATH

The fate of leading textile companies hangs in balance as they await the European Commission (EC) verdict on anti-dumping duty on unbleached fabric exports. The verdict would affect Century Textiles, Mafatlal Industries, Coats Viyella and Vardhaman Spinning Mills. The EC last November imposed provisional anti-dumping duties between five and 17 percent on these companies after an investigation.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS MIGHT TAP NON RESIDENTS' FUNDS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is planning to allow financial institutions to tap non-resident Indian (NRI) funds. This would be the next step towards liberalisation by the RBI to create a level playing-ground for banks and financial institutions. This move was indicated to the Industrial Development Bank of India by the RBI.
MULTINATIONALS TO PICK STAKES IN THREE COMPANIES

Talks between multinationals and Indian promoters are in the final stages for the acquisition of equity stakes in three Indian companies belonging to well known industrial groups. The companies are Nocil, PAL-Peugeot and Lupin Agrochemicals. Sources said talks between the Indian promoters and multinationals were in the final stages in all the three cases. Announcements regarding the acquisition of stakes might come shortly.
INFLATION DECLINES TO 6.35 PERCENT

The annual rate of inflation continued its slide for the seventh week at a stretch to touch 6.35 percent for the week ended April 26. Inflation based on the provisional wholesale price index fell by 0.19 percent points to 6.35 percent from 6.54 percent. Compared to this, inflation was around 4.97 per cent during the corresponding week in April last year.
BOEING, AIRBUS VIE FOR INDIAN AIRLINES ORDER

Close on the heels of the Air-India aircraft deal, Boeing and Airbus were battling it out for Indian Airlines' 50 billion rupee aircraft replacement plan. Both the companies made presentations to the national carrier to bid for twelve 100-seater aircraft and ten 250-seater aircraft which Indian Airlines planned to purchase.
Business Standard
INDIA TO RESIST WORLD TRADE ORGANISATION PRESSURE

India held preliminary bilateral discussions on the financial services sector with all major trading partners in Geneva over the last fortnight. A meeting of World Trade Organisation (WTO) members decided to conclude the negotiations by December 12. But government officials said India was unlikely to gain much from these negotiations. During the last round, India had gained concessions on the movement of natural persons by giving concessions on financial services. Further commitments were now being sought from India on opening up the insurance sector and removing foreign branch limitations.
FOOD SUBSIDY TO UNDERWRITE 25 PCT GOVERNMENT BORROWING

The RBI plans to give six primary dealers the option to underwrite up to 25 percent of the Centre's borrowing programme and link commission to the underwriting commitments. This would help in reducing the commission paid by the RBI, because the commission payable to the primary dealers would be linked to the underwriting commitments and not to the successful bids tendered by them as is currently the practice. This could lead to a situation in which the RBI would not have to pick any devolvement of government papers. The primary dealers were expected to act as market makers in government securities.
FOREIGN INVESTMENT COVER LIKELY FOR INVESTMENT IN HIGHWAYS

The government is considering proposals to hedge foreign investment in the highway sector against the risk of foreign exchange fluctuations. Some foreign investors had suggested that the rate of toll to be charged by the investors be linked to the rupee-dollar exchange rate prevailing at the time of signing the concession agreement. This would ensure that the investors did not stand to lose if the rupee depreciates. Such protection against fluctuation risks would not only give them the anticipated return in dollar terms, but also help them redeem their dollar loans.
INDUSTRIAL GROWTH TO TOUCH 11.5 PCT

The business confidence survey by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) covering over 175 large, medium and small corporate houses indicated the present slow down in the industry was temporary. This trend would be reversed due to the effects of the 1997/98 budget. Industry would grow between 10.5 and 11.5 percent in the first quarter of fiscal 1998/99. The study was based on assumptions such as the rate of borrowing falling to 17 to 18 percent, inflation of around six to seven percent and money supply (M3) being about 15 to 16 percent.
